title: Tension pneumothorax on the vent
learnerTitle: MICU bed 7 — 61M, COPD, RLL pneumonia, ventilated day 2
summary: 61M with COPD ventilated for RLL pneumonia; a left subclavian central line was placed 20 minutes ago. Sudden high airway pressures and desaturation.
objectives: Use peak vs plateau pressure: both up = compliance problem; peak only = resistance problem
Run DOPES: disconnect and bag, check tube, suction, look for pneumothorax
Diagnose tension pneumothorax clinically or by POCUS and decompress before imaging
Treat PEA from an obstructive cause; place a chest tube after decompression

problems: Acute hypercapnic + hypoxemic respiratory failure, intubated (day 2)
Left subclavian CVC placed today (2 needle passes)
chart.hpi: Admitted 2 days ago with RLL pneumonia and COPD exacerbation; failed BiPAP and was intubated. Improving on ceftriaxone/azithromycin. A left subclavian triple-lumen catheter was placed 20 minutes ago for poor peripheral access; the operator reports two passes. Post-procedure CXR not yet done.
chart.pmh: COPD on home tiotropium. 45 pack-year smoker. Hypertension.
chart.social: Retired machinist. Quit smoking 1 year ago.
chart.exam: Before the event: RASS −2, scattered rhonchi R base, equal air entry. Left subclavian dressing clean.

stages.name: Stable on the vent
stages.cue: Baseline. Let the learner review the chart, then trigger the event.

stages.name: Sudden high airway pressures
stages.nurse: The high-pressure alarm keeps going off and he's desatting. His left side isn't moving much.
stages.cue: Ppeak AND Pplat up → compliance problem. Absent left breath sounds, tracheal deviation to the right, distended neck veins. Decompress now.

branches.label: Disconnect and bag, check tube, suction
Orders a chest X-ray or CT first

stages.name: PEA arrest
stages.cue: PEA from obstructive shock. Start CPR and decompress — epinephrine alone will not fix this.

stages.name: Decompressed — chest tube
stages.nurse: Big rush of air. Pressures are coming down.
stages.cue: Place a chest tube, then CXR. Debrief: peak–plateau logic, complication of subclavian access, POCUS signs.

a.text: Portable AP (this morning): ETT 4 cm above the carina. RLL consolidation, improved. No pneumothorax. Hyperinflation.

b.text: Portable AP: Large left pneumothorax with complete lung collapse, mediastinal shift to the right and depression of the left hemidiaphragm — tension physiology. Left subclavian CVC tip in the SVC.

c.text: Portable AP: Large left tension pneumothorax.

d.text: Portable AP: Left chest tube in place; left lung re-expanded with a small residual apical pneumothorax. Mediastinum midline.

b.text: LEFT: no lung sliding anywhere on the anterior chest, no B-lines, barcode sign on M-mode; no lung point found. RIGHT: sliding present.

c.text: LEFT: no lung sliding, barcode sign. RIGHT: sliding present.

d.text: LEFT: lung sliding restored anteriorly; lung point at the apex.

b.text: Inspiratory hold: Ppeak 43, Pplat 38 cmH2O — BOTH elevated (compliance problem, not resistance).
Bagging is very stiff. SpO2 does not improve. No improvement in BP.
Suction catheter passes easily to full depth; scant secretions. Pressures unchanged.
Rush of air on decompression (left 4th/5th ICS, anterior axillary line). BP and SpO2 improving.

chest_tube.text: Left 28 Fr chest tube placed to −20 cmH2O suction; continuous air leak; lung re-expanding.

b.text: Small hyperdynamic LV, compressed RV. IVC plethoric (2.4 cm). No pericardial effusion.

c.text: Organized but weak cardiac activity (pseudo-PEA). No pericardial effusion. IVC plethoric.

b.text: Sinus tachycardia 128. Low-voltage QRS in left precordial leads. No ST elevation.

default.text: Sinus rhythm 92. Right axis. No acute changes.

cta_chest.text: Not performed — patient too unstable to transport (tension physiology on bedside assessment).

ct_chest.text: Not performed — patient too unstable to transport.

teaching: Ppeak ↑ with Pplat ↑ = compliance (pneumothorax, mainstem, edema, abdominal); Ppeak ↑ alone = resistance (plug, kink, bronchospasm, biting).
Tension pneumothorax is a clinical diagnosis; imaging delays treatment.
POCUS: absent sliding + barcode sign supports PTX; lung point confirms; sliding anywhere excludes it at that spot.
Subclavian access carries the highest pneumothorax risk among central line sites; check post-procedure.
